traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 203, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous, with no perianth. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 264 Piperaceae: herbs or shrubs, upright or climbing; leaves usually alternate, entire, rarely opposite or whorled, stalked; stipules joined to the stalk, or none; flowers minute, in dense spikes (sometimes the spikes in umbels), with no perianth; stamens 2 to 6; ovary superior, of one cell with one ovule; fruit a small berry. One carpel is read from the one-celled, one-ovuled ovary (inferred).
